acceptance: Decision gate (what counts as waiting): the wait loops only on the existing `waiting` outcome (every reason matches WAITING_MARKERS). If a pending review verdict or another common wait is classified `refused` today, do not reclassify it here; record the gap as a deferral naming the reason text, so the owner can decide.

Decision gate (API budget): one evaluation makes several GitHub calls. If measuring one evaluation shows more than about 30 calls, lengthen the interval so a 60-minute wait stays under 1,000 calls, and record the measurement in the PR body.
Decision gate (bounds): WAIT must be a positive whole number of minutes with an upper bound (120); anything else is refused with a usage message. Without WAIT behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Decision gate (holds): a held PR (`no-auto-merge`), a refusal, an unresolved thread or a red trunk ends the wait immediately as refused; verify with a test per case that exists in the current refusal list.

Verification: tests/unit/scripts/test_pr_arm.py gains cases with an injected clock and sleeper: waiting then armed arms once; waiting then refused exits refused without further polls; waiting until timeout exits with the waiting code after the expected number of polls; no WAIT makes exactly one evaluation.

Verification: the soundness reviewer's success verdict is recorded for the current head (scripts/pr_arm.py is a soundness path); make pr-preflight passes; make agent-instructions-check passes and AGENTS.md stays within 17,300 bytes and 170 lines.
Verification: `make help` shows WAIT; docs/agent/merge-authority.md states the outcome prefix, exit codes, interval and maximum.
Done when the PR is merged to develop. After the merge, arm the next PR in this set with WAIT and record in the umbrella item whether it behaved as specified.
description:
Source: a retrospective over 25 agent sessions (2026-10-18 to 2026-11-11), followed by an adversarial re-check of each claim against origin/develop 4835f5a537.

Problem. AGENTS.md says 'Check CI on a schedule, never in a loop', yet close-out needs `make pr-arm` to be repeated until the PR is armable. Sessions wrote at least 61 shell polling loops, each grepping a different string. One exited after 6 seconds on an unmatched message, one syntax error cost about an hour, and scratch watcher scripts in /tmp were lost twice. Concurrent loops may also have exhausted the GitHub API quota once (inferred, not proven).

Owner decision 2026-11-11: add `make pr-arm WAIT=<minutes>`. It polls at a fixed interval, loops only while the outcome is `waiting`, and exits at once on armed or refused. Reword AGENTS.md so this is the one allowed wait.

Change. scripts/pr_arm.py: a wait option (make variable WAIT, minutes) that re-evaluates until the outcome is not `waiting` or the time runs out; on timeout it exits with the existing waiting exit code and says so. One fixed interval between polls, defined once, no shorter than two minutes. Durations use benchbox.utils.clock where the script may import it, otherwise time.monotonic. make/pr-landing.mk passes WAIT through; make/help.mk documents it. docs/agent/merge-authority.md documents the outcome contract (`pr-arm: outcome: waiting|refused|armed` and exit codes) and the wait. AGENTS.md 'Verification and close-out': replace 'Check CI on a schedule, never in a loop' with wording that names `make pr-arm WAIT=` as the supported wait and still forbids hand-written loops.

Non-goals. No change to what arms or refuses. No wait mode for pr-arm-remote, pr-ready or pr-rerun. No automatic rerun, rebase, stand-in or hold change while waiting.

This item changes the close-out loop itself, so it is delivered serially and cannot be used to arm its own PR in wait mode as evidence.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone, and pass absolute worktree paths to every file tool; stage paths explicitly, never git add -A; no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); heavy work only via make heavy-run, never forcing admission or skipping the test lock; never bypass a required check, ruleset, hold label or review gate, and never post a stand-in; change only the files this item names, and report anything else as noticed-but-not-touched; re-read every cited file on current origin/develop before editing, because the line numbers here are hints from 2026-11-11 (origin/develop 4835f5a537); close at a merged PR (make pr-open, make pr-arm), and finish this item only after the merge is observed.
